questions.q: What is the difference between upsampling and downsampling?
options: Upsampling goes to a finer step and creates new rows; downsampling goes to a coarser step and merges rows
They are two names for the same thing
why: Correct. Hourly to daily is downsampling. Daily to hourly is upsampling.

questions.q: Which aggregation for daily rainfall (mm) when you need monthly data?
why: Correct. Monthly rain is the total of the days.
last gives only the final day.

questions.q: Hourly sales: 4, 6, 5, 9. What is the sum for these 4 hours? And what would mean give? Enter the sum.
A price list changes on the 1st of each month. You build daily features for a model that predicts tomorrow. Which fill?
why: Correct. The price stays the same until the next change, and ffill never looks ahead.
bfill uses the next month's price on earlier days: leakage.
interpolate invents prices between months and uses the future.

questions.q: Daily data starts on Monday. You run s.resample('W').sum() and the last row looks 60% lower than the rest. What is the most likely cause?
why: Correct. A partial last bin has fewer days. Drop it or mark it.
sum is the right choice for flows.

questions.q: 5-minute bins with default settings. A row has the timestamp 10:10. Which bin label does it get?
why: Correct. Closed left: the bin [10:10, 10:15) is named 10:10.
That bin holds 10:05 up to, but not including, 10:10.
Labels are the left edge by default.

questions.q: A bank balance is reported daily. The business wants monthly data. Which aggregation?
why: Correct. The balance at month end is the monthly value.
Summing balances counts the same money many times.
That is not a standard choice and has no meaning for a stock.
